headline: Agreed on corrective measures for Mixx 360 after assault and crowd-control incidents on July 25, 2026
summary: The Board held a hearing on police reports describing an assault, crowd control problems, and a request for mutual aid at Mixx 360 on July 25, 2026. Owner Anthony Decotis accepted responsibility for the incident. The Board and Mr. Decotis agreed to a list of corrective measures covering police details, staff training, security procedures, signage, and camera coverage, rather than taking license action.
decisions: The Board and Mr. Decotis agreed to corrective measures instead of taking license action, including requesting police details for Friday and Saturday events, additional security training, strengthened incident procedures, no re-entry signage, continued bag checks, event review and cancellation when needed, improved camera coverage, and attention to parking lot congestion.

plain_text:
CITY OF MALDEN
MASSACHUSETTS
Liquor Licensing Board
Meeting Minutes
Date: August 18 , 2026
        Time: 6:00 PM
Members in Attendance :                           Also in Attendance:
Kevin Molis- Chairman Gia Finocchiaro
Denise Balboni-Cowie Cpt Paul Hopkins
Andrew Zieberg
Meeting Called to Order:  6:00 PM
Called to Order By: Kevin Molis
Seconded By: Denise Balboni-Cowie
The following were considered for approval:
1. The Licensing Board held a hearing concerning Mixx 360 located at 665 
Broadway, to determine whether any action should be taken regarding its 
liquor, entertainment license. The hearing was prompted by several 
police reports concerning incidents that occurred on the nights of July 18, 
2026, and July 25, 2026.
The Board focused primarily on an event hosted by an outside promoter 
on July 25. According to the police reports:
 A Mixx 360 employee was assaulted by a patron.
 Multiple altercations reportedly occurred inside and outside the 
establishment.
 A large crowd became difficult to control as the event ended.
 The parking lot and entrances became congested, creating concerns 
regarding emergency vehicle access and crowd management.
 Due to the situation, Malden Police requested mutual aid from surrounding
communities and State Police to help disperse the crowd.
 Police reports indicated a large crowd.
 Concerns were also raised about patrons smoking inside and about the 
overall ability of security personnel to manage the crowd.
Anthony Decotis, owner/license holder of Mixx 360, acknowledged the 
facts contained in the police reports and accepted full responsibility for 
the problems that occurred.
He explained that:
 He has operated the business for approximately 30 years and considers 
responsible management and community relations extremely important.
 Mixx 360 has increasingly hosted multicultural events with Brazilian, 
Colombian, Cape Verdean, Jamaican, and other promoters.
 The July 25 event was different from the typical Jamaican events Mixx 360
had previously hosted and resulted in an unusually difficult crowd.
 He acknowledged that he approved the event and stated that he ultimately
considers the incident his responsibility.
 Mixx 360 had approximately eight security personnel working that night, all
of whom were Mixx 360 employees rather than security provided by the 
outside promoter.
 The establishment has an occupancy capacity of approximately 800–850,
but the owner stated that the business generally tries to keep crowds 
below that level for better crowd flow.
 The business ended the event early when management recognized that 
the situation was deteriorating.
 Mr. Decotis stated that several future events had already been cancelled 
or reconsidered because of concerns about the promoters or anticipated 
crowds.
The Board questioned how security handled the employee assault.
Mr. Decotis explained that security:
 Removed the individual from the immediate area and kept him in a back
room.
 Contacted police.
 Took a photograph of the individual and believed they had his identifying 
information.
 Ultimately allowed the individual to leave because security was concerned 
that physically restraining him could escalate the situation, particularly 
because he was accompanied by other individuals.
The Board discussed the uncertainty security personnel may have 
regarding what they are legally permitted to do when a person needs to be
identified or held until police arrive.
The Board suggested that additional security training would be beneficial, 
particularly regarding:
 Handling physical altercations.
 When and how to involve police.
 Identifying individuals involved in incidents.
 Preserving information such as identification and vehicle information.
 Managing crowds and potentially dangerous situations.
 The Board strongly emphasized the value of having a police detail present 
during larger events.
 Mr. Decotis explained that Mixx 360 frequently requests police details but 
that the requests are not always filled. He stated that the business 
normally uses police details on Saturdays but had not requested one for 
the July 25 Friday event because Fridays are typically slower.
 The Board’s expectation going forward was that Mixx 360 should request a
police detail for Friday and Saturday events regardless of whether the 
request can ultimately be filled.
 The discussion ultimately centered around requesting details 
approximately 11:00 p.m. to 3:00 a.m., recognizing that the police 
department cannot always guarantee that an officer will be available.
The Board expressed concern about the parking lot becoming congested 
during large events. Specific concerns included:
 Vehicles blocking entrances and exits.
 Difficulty for police, fire, or ambulance personnel to access the property.
 Patrons congregating near the entrances.
 The need for better traffic direction during large events.
Mr. Decotis stated that Mixx 360 already has personnel directing traffic but 
acknowledged that additional attention may be necessary during particularly 
challenging events.
The Board also discussed security procedures concerning bags and patrons 
leaving and attempting to return to the establishment.
Mr. Decotis stated that Mix 360 has implemented and is strengthening 
procedures concerning:
 Bag checks.
 Wanding patrons/ Metal detectors
 ID checks.
 Preventing patrons from returning to their vehicles and then re-entering.
 Preventing patrons from bringing outside alcohol into the establishment.
The Board recommended that visible signage be posted informing patrons 
that once they leave the establishment, they cannot return.
In Conclusion the Board and Mr. Decotis agreed that the incidents that 
occurred were serious and created significant public-safety concerns. The 
board recognized Mr. Decotis’s long history of responsible operations, his 
willingness to acknowledge the problems and agree to suggestions and 
corrective actions. The Board pointed out that the police reports did not 
indicate concerns about overserving alcohol and exceeding the licensed 
capacity. The primary concern was the altercations, the crowd
behavior/management and the resources exhausted by the Malden Police 
and Mutual aid requested.
The corrective measures that are to be taken/put forth are:
1. Request police details for Friday and Saturday events, particularly during 
late-night hours. Working toward a 11:00 p.m.–3:00 a.m. detail 
window when available.
2. Provide additional training for Mixx 360 security and staff.
3. Strengthen procedures for handling altercations and identifying individuals 
involved in incidents. Improve documentation, including obtaining 
identification and vehicle information when appropriate.
4. Post signage stating that patrons cannot leave and return to the 
establishment.
5. Continue and strengthen bag checks and security screening.
6. Continue reviewing and cancelling events when Mixx 360 cannot 
adequately assess the promoter, crowd, or potential risks.
7. Continue evaluating and improving security camera coverage. The owner 
stated that additional cameras had already been installed following the 
July 25 incident.
8. Pay particular attention to parking lot congestion and emergency 
access during large events.
Meeting adjourned at :
Time: 7:05 PM
Motion By: Denise Baldoni-Cowie
Seconded By: Andrew Zeiberg
Minutes respectfully submitted by : Gia Finocchiaro – Liquor Licensing Clerk
